text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Figures from parliamentary drug inquiry commission show number of foreigners involved in drug traffic in Morocco in 1995 totalled 316 out of 19,331 arrests, compared with 262 among 11,949 arrests in 1994.
- King Hassan, to mark 53rd anniversary of Independance Manifesto, grants full or partial pardons to 1,401 people serving prison sentences or having been fined.
- Three student leaders arrested on charge of disturbing public order, linked to protest marches over student transport for university in Casablanca.
- One fifth of urban community families and one-tenth of those in countryside are affected by unemployment of at least one family member.
- Former commander in Polisario says leaders seizing food aid sent to camps and selling it for personal profit.
- Four bodies and seven injured recovered from coach that plunged into river, but rescue services expect toll to rise.
- U.N. committee for elimination of discrimination against women is soon to examine initial report on Morocco.
